summary: Using Pick Block on boats crashes the game
description: I know that this is duplicated with but MAY I help you tell the reason? Description 1. Place a boat, any variant. 2. Switch to creative mode. 3. Middle-click the boat, and you ll find that it crashes. Reason "class cqh" (Boat) has a function "cvx cqh.dK()" (Boat.getPickResult). That returns a new "class cvx"(ItemStack) of function "cvt cqh.al_()" (Boat.getDropItem). "cvt cqh.al_()" (Boat.getDropItem) returns "cqh$b cqh.w()" (Boat.getVariant) s "cvt cqh$b.d()" (Boat$Type.getBoat) . And it seemed like "cvt cqh$b.d()" returns null, then "cvx. (deu, int, ku)" (ItemStack(ItemLike, int, PatchedDataComponentMap)) crashes.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Place a boat in your world.
2. Switch to Creative mode.
3. Middle-click on the boat.
4. Observe that the game crashes after middle-clicking the boat.
Observed Behavior: When using the pick block function on a boat in Minecraft, the game crashes under specific conditions. To reproduce this issue, first place any variant of a boat. Then switch to creative mode and attempt to middle-click the boat using the pick block feature. This action will cause the game to crash. The root cause lies within the "class cqh" (Boat) which has a function called "cvx cqh.dK()" (Boat.getPickResult). This function is designed to return an ItemStack, but it relies on another function "cvt cqh.al_()" (Boat.getDropItem), which in turn depends on "cqh$b cqh.w()" (Boat.getVariant) and subsequently "cvt cqh$b.d()" (Boat$Type.getBoat). The issue arises because "cvt cqh$b.d()" returns null, leading to a crash when the ItemStack constructor is called with these parameters. This indicates that there is an unexpected null value being passed into a method where it should not be allowed, causing the game to terminate abruptly.
Expected Behavior: When middle-clicking (using Pick Block) on a boat in creative mode, the game should not crash. Instead, it should successfully pick up the boat as an item in the inventory without any issues or errors. This action should work consistently for all types of boats and should not cause any unexpected behavior or crashes.
